table.reasoning: Both switch on a status String and return a system image name. Shared cases: 'completed' -> 'checkmark.circle.fill', 'in_progress' -> 'circle.dotted.circle', default -> 'circle'. taskIcon adds a 'deleted' case. Same algorithm, same type, one extra case — STRUCTURAL duplication.

Both switch on a status String and return a Color. Shared cases: 'completed' -> .green, 'in_progress' -> .orange, default -> .secondary. taskColor adds a 'deleted' -> .red case. Same algorithm, same type, one extra case — STRUCTURAL duplication.

Both inline the identical expression: dict.sorted(by: { $0.key < $1.key }).map { "\($0.key): \($0.value)" }.joined(separator: "\n") to format a [String: String] dictionary into a display string. The expression is copy-pasted verbatim.

Both follow the same algorithm: (1) split content into lines, (2) check a line-count threshold, (3) if exceeded render a fallback layout using ToolResultView, (4) otherwise render an inline diff with per-line monospaced Text rows, a colored foreground, per-line background, and an outer container with textSelection + padding + background. The structural scaffolding — threshold guard, fallback branch, per-line ForEach rendering, container modifiers — is identical. The only differences are the number of content arrays (two for edit, one for write) and the prefix characters/colors per array.

table.pattern: TaskListItem status -> (icon: String, color: Color) mapping. The bidirectional status-string-to-presentation mapping (icon name + tint color) is implemented twice inside LogViewerView (todoIcon/todoColor for the todo checklist, taskIcon/taskColor for the task panel), and is not extracted into a shared, reusable abstraction.
table.reuse_potential: High. Any view that renders a TaskListItem row needs the same icon and color for the same status strings. SubagentDetailView or future task-related views would duplicate this mapping again without an extraction.

findings.title: todoIcon/todoColor duplicated by taskIcon/taskColor
findings.issue: todoIcon(_:) (line 932) and taskIcon(_:) (line 1267) implement the same status-string-to-system-image algorithm. todoColor(_:) (line 940) and taskColor(_:) (line 1276) implement the same status-string-to-Color algorithm. Both pairs are STRUCTURAL duplications — same switch structure, same cases, same return values, with taskIcon/taskColor adding one extra 'deleted' case.
findings.impact: Any change to shared status presentation (e.g., renaming the icon for 'in_progress') must be applied in two places. The two implementations will inevitably diverge.
findings.rule_source: DRY-2: Inlined Duplication — same logical sequence in multiple locations

findings.title: Dictionary-to-display-string expression duplicated in mcpDetailView and toolExpandedContent
findings.issue: The expression `dict.sorted(by: { $0.key < $1.key }).map { "\($0.key): \($0.value)" }.joined(separator: "\n")` appears verbatim at line 703 (toolExpandedContent .other branch) and again at lines 785-788 (mcpDetailView). This is an IDENTICAL duplication of a formatting expression on [String: String] input.
findings.impact: Any formatting change (e.g., separator, sort order, key-value delimiter) must be applied in both locations. The expression is not named, making its intent non-obvious at both call sites.
findings.rule_source: DRY-2: Inlined Duplication — identical logic in 2+ locations

findings.title: editDiffView and writeDiffView share the same diff-rendering algorithm
findings.issue: editDiffView(_:) (lines 712-769) and writeDiffView(_:) (lines 873-911) implement the same structural algorithm: threshold check -> fallback-to-ToolResultView branch -> inline per-line ForEach rendering with monospaced font, colored foreground, per-line background highlight, and outer container modifiers. This is a STRUCTURAL duplication — the same algorithm applied to slightly different data shapes.
findings.impact: Changes to the diff rendering presentation (container styling, font size, threshold value, fallback behavior) must be applied to both methods. The duplication will grow as more tool types with file-content rendering are added.
findings.rule_source: DRY-2: Inlined Duplication — same algorithm with different concrete types

findings.title: TaskListItem status-to-presentation mapping not extracted as a shared abstraction
findings.issue: The mapping from a TaskListItem status string to a system icon name and a Color is implemented twice inside LogViewerView: once for the todo checklist (todoIcon/todoColor, lines 932-946) and once for the task panel (taskIcon/taskColor, lines 1267-1283). This is a generic presentation pattern — mapping a domain status value to its visual representation — that is not domain-specific to either rendering context and should be extracted as a standalone reusable abstraction (e.g., a static method or extension on TaskListItem, or a TaskStatusPresentation value type).
findings.impact: Any view that renders TaskListItem rows must re-implement the same mapping. The two in-file implementations already diverge (taskIcon adds 'deleted'). Further divergence is likely as more status values are added.
findings.rule_source: DRY-3: Missing Abstraction — generic pattern not extracted for reuse
